newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVE'S BOKSIC TO VISIT TAPIE IN PRISON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVE'S BOKSIC TO VISIT TAPIE IN PRISON.

text.p: Former Olympique Marseille striker Alen Boksic, now with Italy's Juventus, said he would visit the French club's ex-chairman Bernard Tapie in prison, a newspaper reported on Saturday.
"I'm sorry about my former boss, but we knew it would end up like this," Croatian Boksic told the Tuttosport daily.
"I think I will go and visit him in jail," he added.
Former politician Tapie, 56, entered central Paris's La Sante prison on Monday to begin an eight-month sentence for rigging a first division soccer match between Marseille and Valenciennes in 1993.
That match was played just before Boksic helped Marseille beat AC Milan to win the European Cup final.
"I have an excellent relationship with Tapie," said Boksic, who is expected to return to play in a month after injuring an ankle in a league match on January 12.

"We talked in Paris (before he went to jail) and he told me, 'Alen, I've got to go now. Sooner or later it's going to be my turn'. He's a great person and has lived the experiences of 10 men put together.
"He treated me very well at Marseille and I am grateful for that -- that's why I will visit him in jail."
